sentences.text: High water and low water are the highest and lowest levels in each tide cycle, and the range is the difference between them.
Charted depths are measured from mean lower low water, so the actual depth at any moment equals the charted depth plus the height of tide.
A tide height can be negative, meaning the water is below mean lower low water and shallower than charted.
That happens around spring tides, especially with strong offshore winds.
The stand of the tide is the brief period at high or low water when the level barely changes.
